sentences.text: 1. In this appeal, the accused/appellant (hereinafter referred to as 'accused') has challenged the judgment dated 17.03.2017 and the order on sentence dated 28.07.2017 passed by the Ld. Trial Court in case FIR No.348/2004, PS. Badarpur, titled as "State Vs. Gautam Singh" whereby the accused was convicted under Section 279/337/304-A of IPC.

He was sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- as compensation to the victim, in default of payment of fine, he was to further undergo simple imprisonment for a period of two months for the offence punishable under section 304-A IPC; to Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 1 Of 8 undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months and to pay a fine of Rs.500/-, in default of payment of fine, he was to further undergo simple imprisonment for a period of seven days for the offence punishable under Section 337 IPC;
and to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default of payment of fine, he was to further undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 30 days for the offence punishable under Section 279 IPC.
The sentences were to run concurrently and benefit of Section 428 of Cr.PC was to be given to the accused.

2. Shorn of unnecessary details, alleged facts of the case are that on 18.05.2004 at about 1:00 AM,
the accused was driving the vehicle bearing No. DL-1VB-0288, at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner due to which it overturned, injuring the passengers sitting therein and due to the said injury son of the complaint died.

1
An FIR was registered regarding the incident and after completion of investigation, the charge sheet was filed against the accused under Section 279/338/304-A IPC.
The charge under Section 279/337/338/304-A IPC was framed against the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
3. During trial, prosecution examined eight witnesses to prove its case.

After conclusion of the trial,
Ld. Trial Court convicted and sentenced the accused vide impugned judgment and order on sentence.
4. Accused has challenged the impugned order primarily on Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 2 Of 8 the ground that the Ld. Trial Court has passed the judgment without proper appreciation of the evidence.

entities.text: Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 2 Of 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Counsel for the accused argued that:
(i) The accused had applied brakes to save the passengers on board and not the dog,
as held by the Ld. trial court, because hitting the dog would have been fatal to the passengers.

He argued that the appellant was conscious of the risk of running over the dog, hence, he applied brakes suddenly and took a sharp turn due to which the vehicle got disbalanced and over turned, resulting into injuries to the passenger in the vehicle and unfortunate death of infant child of 14 months.
(ii) PW1 has said in his testimony that the vehicle was being driven at a high speed but driving the vehicle merely at high speed does not amount to being 'rash and negligent'.
Even otherwise, the vehicle was not being driven at high speed as PW1 has not testified about the speed of the vehicle.
He deposed that he had no idea about the speed of the vehicle.
(iii) PW2 said that the accused had consumed liquor but there is no MLC in this regard.
Moreover, PW1 did not say anything on this aspect.
(iv) The accused cannot be convicted only because an accident had happened causing death of a person, despite the fact that the accused was not rash and negligent in driving the vehicle.
(v) The Ld. Trial Court could have taken the other view favourable to the accused as there is no material on record leading to the conclusion that the accused was negligent while driving the vehicle.
(vi) He also argued that had the vehicle been driven at a very high speed all the passengers must have sustained the fatal injuries.

However, the other passengers sustained only simple injuries, which indicates that the speed of the vehicle was not uncontrolled but due to sudden application of the brakes the vehicle lost control and Gautam Singh vs The State on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30696729/
2 turned over.

sentences.text: 6. I have heard the arguments advanced by the Ld. Addl. PP Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 3 Of 8 for the State and by Ld. Counsel for the appellant and have also gone through the Ld. Trial Court record.

entities.text: Ld. Addl. PP Gautam Singh Vs. State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. In order to prove the commission of offence punishable under Section 279/337/304A of IPC,
following ingredients are required to be proved:-
(i) The identity of the offender i.e., it was he, who was driving the offending vehicle on the spot, which was a public way.
(ii) Rashness or negligence i.e., the offender was driving his vehicle in such a manner,
which amounted to rash or negligent and caused the death of the victim due to such an act.
8.
In the present case, admittedly, the accused had been driving the vehicle and does not need appreciation of evidence on this aspect.
It also becomes clear from the suggestions given to PW1/complainant during his cross examination.

During his cross examinations, it was suggested to him that the accused was not driving the vehicle at the fast speed while returning and that the accused had applied sudden brakes for saving a dog, who had come infront of the vehicle.
Hence, it is clear that the accused had been driving the vehicle in question on a public way.
9. Now, it is to be seen, if the accused was driving the vehicle in such a manner, which amounted to rash or negligent and caused the death of the complainant's son due to such an act.

10. Counsel for the accused argued that the accused had suddenly applied brakes after seeing a dog on the road, because Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 4 Of 8 hitting the dog could have been fatal to the passengers.

entities.text: Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 4 Of 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also argued that though PW1 has said in his testimony that the vehicle was being driven at a high speed yet driving the vehicle merely at high speed does not amount to being 'rash and negligent' and even otherwise PW1 has not testified about the speed of the vehicle, he deposed that he had no idea about the speed of the vehicle.
11. Ld. Trial Court has observed in the judgment that the accused was a professional driver as he was driving the taxi which was hired for driving to different states.
Therefore, the accused must have possessed proficiency in driving and would have been able to anticipate possible conditions arising on the road and to control the vehicle in such situations.

12. In Deota Misir vs. Emperor, AIR 1931 All 708, the Ld. Trial Court had convicted the accused for causing death of a person by doing a rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide on the facts that the accused was the driver of a motor lorry and was driving his lorry fast and hence the lorry collided with a tree, due to which the lorry overturned and one of the passengers was killed and some were injured.

entities.text: Deota Misir vs. Emperor, AIR 1931 All 708
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:

3
The accused denied that he was driving fast or that he was guilty of any negligence.

His defence was that he saw two bullock carts coming towards him in the middle of the road, he intended to pass on his own left in the ordinary way, but the bullock-cart drivers took their carts one to the right and one to the left, and being unable to pass on his own left he swerved in order to try and pass on the right,
and so struck the tree.
Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 5 Of 8

In the said case, Hon'ble Allahabad High Court upheld the conviction of the accused observing that every driver in India knows that villagers are not sufficiently alive to the rules of traffic and he also knows that he may at any moment find drivers of bullock-carts or carts on the wrong side of the road, particularly on country roads and he knows that bullock-cart drivers may turn on to their wrong side of the road when they see traffic approaching.

Hon'ble Allahabad High Court held that had the accused been driving at a pace at which he had his lorry under proper control, he should have been able to stop it at any time to avoid an accident without resorting to the dangerous expedient of swinging his car off to the wrong side of the road.

Hon'ble High Court also held that while there was negligence undoubtedly on the part of one of the bullock-cart drivers, the accused, if he had his lorry under proper control, should have been able to avoid the consequences of that negligence.
His negligence therefore, was the negligence that substantially caused the accident.

13. In the instant case as well, it is the defence of the accused is that he had been driving the vehicle at a moderate speed and with due care and caution but he had to apply brakes suddenly because a dog had come on the road and hitting the dog could have been fatal to the passengers.
Vehicle drivers know very well that while driving a vehicle on road something may come in the way all of a sudden, especially stray animals.

Therefore, a driver has to drive his vehicle, taking such precaution that if something of such sort Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 6 Of 8 happens and he has to either suddenly apply the brakes or swerve the vehicle, the vehicle always must remain under his control.

entities.text: Gautam Singh Vs. State Page 6 Of 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the present case also, had the accused been driving the vehicle at a speed, he had been able to keep the vehicle under proper control, he could have comfortably been able to stop the vehicle,
safely, at a distance from the dog to avoid an accident due to collision, as argued by the counsel,
without resorting to the dangerous consequence of overturning the vehicle.

His negligence,
therefore, was the negligence that caused the accident due to which the vehicle overturned causing injuries to the passengers and death of the son of the complainant.
14. Ex.PW8/X is the mechanical inspection report of the vehicle and in the cross examination of PW8 no contradiction has been brought to impeach the authenticity of the said report.
Perusal of this report clearly shows the damage suffered by the vehicle in the accident.
The damages suffered by the vehicle also indicates that the vehicle must have overturned violently and which is only possible if, the vehicle is driven in a rash and negligent manner.

Gautam Singh vs The State on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30696729/
4 15.
As per the MLCs of the injured persons, the injuries were suffered by the passengers in a road traffic accident.
Further, in the post mortem report of the deceased/Ex.PW7/A, it is mentioned that death was caused due to the ante mortem injuries suffered by blunt force, possible in a road traffic accident.

16. Having discussed as above, it stands established that the accused/appellant had been driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner due to which it overturned causing injury to passengers and to a 14 months old child, causing his death.
Gautam Singh
Vs. State Page 7 Of 8 17.
Therefore, this court finds that the Ld. Trial Court was justified in convicting the appellant/accused.
Hence, no merit in this appeal and the same is accordingly dismissed.
18. TCR be sent back along with a copy of this order.
File be consigned to record room, as per rules.

(Subhash Kumar Mishra)
